title: Unfinished Seal — proposal
open: A valid certificate requires every named institution’s fresh authorization of the same artifact, ceremony identifier, and expiry.
status: Withdrawal, missing assent, and replay need exact semantics. The certificate establishes digital participation, not sincerity or physical presence.
why: Shared civic symbols whose authenticated creation requires a cooperative act.

title: Unattributed Veto Liturgy — proposal
open: Institutions submit private constraints over an agreed vocabulary of gestures and utterances. Release one acceptable ceremony or a single failure symbol.
status: Theological acceptability requires agreed predicates; repeated feasibility queries can expose another institution’s taboos.
why: Joint rites across incompatible traditions without turning private boundaries into bargaining ammunition.
key_works: SPDZ; collaborative proofs over distributed witnesses.

title: Chorus Without a Master — proposal
open: Private motifs produce a common score satisfying contribution, duration, and balance rules. The eventual performance is explicitly authorized disclosure.
status: Local parts may imply other parts. Motif extraction, covert messages, and rehearsal metadata require analysis.
why: A cultural work whose first complete public realization requires cooperation.

title: Reciprocal Silence — proposal
open: Release one completion bit for anonymous community quorums and approved acoustic predicates; raw audio and individual attendance are not submitted to computing institutions.
status: Sensor signatures establish provenance, not truthful measurement. Cameras, small quorums, and known attendance can defeat anonymity.
why: Joint mourning or silence observances without a shared attendee register.
key_works: Coconut credentials; Prio’s validated private aggregation.

title: Many Tongues, One Oath — proposal
open: Each institution authorizes private wording and an approved translation into a common formal obligation schema. Public output certifies equality of those obligations.
status: The translation’s legitimacy remains a human agreement; cryptography cannot prove unrestricted semantic equivalence.
why: Shared operational commitments that preserve distinct religious and historical vocabularies.
key_works: Collaborative zk-SNARKs over distributed private inputs.

title: Withdrawable Communion — proposal
open: A ritual completes only if current, unrevoked consent satisfies every required community quorum; no withdrawer list is released.
status: Timing, compromised devices, or nearly known quorums can expose a withdrawal. Secret consent cannot prove freedom from physical coercion.
why: Collective ceremonies whose digital legitimacy includes an individual right to leave.
key_works: Coconut; malicious MPC over private state.

title: No-Humiliation Ceremony — proposal
open: A ceremony must remain below every submitted burden cap and meet each participant’s declared minimum benefit.
status: Actors can exaggerate burdens. The missing mechanism-design result is truthful elicitation compatible with privacy and voluntary participation.
why: Cooperation without requiring public admission of which gestures feel humiliating or costly.
key_works: MPC implementations of private economic mechanisms.

title: Indispensable Hand — proposal
open: For each honest role retaining an independently sampled hidden seed, all other roles together cannot predict the canonical session digest before its authorized contribution.
status: Binding a seed does not prove its entropy or prevent voluntary disclosure. Adaptive inputs and abort selection require a contributiveness reduction.
why: Rituals with a precise property of indispensable cooperation.
key_works: Distributed key generation; adversarial coin-flipping limits.

title: Answerless Census — proposal
subfield: Censuses without institutional access to individual answers
open: Respondents secret-share answers directly from their own devices; institutions receive only a fixed collection of privacy-protected statistics.
status: Compromised devices, fraudulent enrollment, and coercive collection remain. Exact tiny-cell outputs can reveal individual responses.
why: A census jointly auditable by rival institutions without making them repositories of vulnerable people’s answers.

title: Minority Need Without a Roll — proposal
subfield: Censuses without institutional access to individual answers
open: For a predeclared region, release a privacy-protected decision about sufficient demand, withholding names and exact prevalence.
status: Exact thresholds conflict with strong individual privacy. Service policy must tolerate calibrated uncertainty near the threshold.
why: Language, accessibility, or worship accommodations without exposing everyone who needs them.
key_works: Prio aggregation; differentially private query release.

title: Many Registers, One Person — proposal
subfield: Censuses without institutional access to individual answers
open: Compute deduplicated population statistics while withholding record matches and the merged roster from every institution.
status: Aliases, missing documents, and uncertain identity matches are substantive problems. Ambiguous matches require bounds, rather than treating equality as proof of personhood.
why: Censuses across disputed administrations, refugee agencies, and overlapping service systems.

title: No-Trajectory Population Clock — proposal
subfield: Censuses without institutional access to individual answers
open: Publish coarse, budgeted changes across time while keeping arrivals, departures, locations, and cross-epoch linkages hidden.
status: Individually modest releases can collectively expose trajectories. Renewal, repeated windows, and lifelong composition need a unified privacy model.
why: Planning for mobile or displaced populations without an institutional movement register.

title: Protected Nonresponse Audit — proposal
subfield: Censuses without institutional access to individual answers
open: Estimate coverage and nonresponse across approved coarse strata, releasing uncertainty intervals rather than nonparticipant lists.
status: Coverage models depend on assumptions about sampling and dependence. Hostile collectors can coordinate omissions or fabricate apparently independent frames.
why: Evidence of systematic undercounting without making nonrespondents easier to target.

title: Disagreement-Preserving Census — proposal
subfield: Censuses without institutional access to individual answers
open: Institutions commit competing finite classification rules; the census releases privacy-protected statistical ranges across those rules, without individual labels.
status: Arbitrary recodings can become identifying queries. The taxonomy family and its joint sensitivity must be fixed before responses arrive.
why: Service planning despite disagreement about language, affiliation, ethnicity, or jurisdiction.

title: Betrayal-Bounded Census — proposal
subfield: Censuses without institutional access to individual answers
open: Respondents locally randomize answers before sharing them. Reconstructing all stored reports subsequently reveals only locally private observations.
status: Local privacy reduces accuracy and requires trustworthy respondent randomness. Unlimited repeated reports consume the guarantee; outside knowledge remains.
why: Census confidentiality that does not depend entirely on permanent institutional independence.
key_works: Warner’s randomized response; Prio; differential privacy.

title: Household Without a Head — proposal
subfield: Censuses without institutional access to individual answers
open: Members independently submit attributes and co-residence claims; release a privacy-protected household distribution rather than combined forms.
status: Malicious relationship claims alter graph sensitivity. The construction needs a bounded-household model and a workable correction process.
why: Census participation that preserves individual agency inside families and shared accommodation.

title: Winner Without a Tally — proposal
subfield: Elections that reveal only the authorized outcome
open: Under a fixed plurality rule and tie-breaker, release only the winner or prescribed no-result symbol.
status: Enrollment, voter intent, coercion resistance, and receipt-free inclusion remain separate. Known ballots plus the winner can still reveal information.
why: Leadership selection without disclosing factional strength or defeat margins.

title: Sealed Elimination Election — proposal
subfield: Elections that reveal only the authorized outcome
open: Publish only the final winner; hide intermediate tallies, transfer patterns, exhaustion counts, and candidate elimination order.
status: Timing and proof shape must not expose rounds. Fractional transfer rules need exact arithmetic, not implementation-dependent floating point.
why: Preference aggregation without publishing fragile coalition relationships.

title: Cross-Community Mandate — proposal
subfield: Elections that reveal only the authorized outcome
open: Elect the rule-selected candidate only if hidden membership-linked ballots satisfy agreed support floors.
status: Membership certification is a constitutional choice. Strategic candidate sets and repeated elections can reveal hidden support even when each transcript is private.
why: Power-sharing elections without sectarian electoral maps.

title: Hidden-Turnout Mandate — proposal
subfield: Elections that reveal only the authorized outcome
open: Release a winner if valid participation meets the quorum; otherwise release the prescribed no-result symbol. Exact turnout and precinct breakdowns are withheld.
status: Polling observation and network traffic may reveal participation. The quorum result itself necessarily conveys threshold information.
why: Participation requirements without exposing abstention patterns.

title: Marginless Recount — proposal
subfield: Elections that reveal only the authorized outcome
open: Recompute a frozen election and release only confirmation of the certified winner or an inconsistency verdict.
status: Agreement between implementations does not prove voter intent. Shared bugs, common preprocessing, and common input-validation errors remain.
why: Meaningful computational challenges without acquiring population-level intelligence.

title: Unexposed Nomination — proposal
subfield: Elections that reveal only the authorized outcome
open: Voters rank a public universe of eligible people; only privately authenticated, consenting nominees are considered. Reveal the winner alone.
status: Large candidate universes are burdensome. The winner constrains the hidden nomination set, and nominee communications may expose choices.
why: Leadership recruitment where standing, declining, or losing invites retaliation.

title: Silent-Exit Delegation — proposal
subfield: Elections that reveal only the authorized outcome
open: Permit private delegation, revocation, or overriding ballots under fixed cycle and delegation-cap rules; publish only the winner.
status: Cycle semantics, recovery, update races, and graph-scale costs need precise treatment. Device control can defeat private revocation.
why: Representative decision-making without a public map of loyalty and withdrawal.

title: Unreportable Ballot — proposal
subfield: Elections that reveal only the authorized outcome
open: Under private-registration and safe-voting assumptions, a voter may use a decoy credential or override a coerced submission; decisive ballots remain unclassified publicly.
status: An unobserved registration or voting opportunity remains essential. Cryptography cannot manufacture privacy under continuous physical or client surveillance.
why: Winner-only elections with a carefully specified avenue for resisting coercion.

title: Split-Voice Testimony Channel — proposal
open: Receiving authorized testimony grants neither contactability nor identification power; each relationship requires a separate policy.
status: Adaptive corruption and cross-policy linkage require composition proofs. Stylometry, disclosed facts, or a compromised endpoint can identify the speaker.
why: Evidence contribution without surrendering permanent contact or identification capabilities.

title: Contradiction-Preserving Testimony Bundles — proposal
open: Release every admitted, consented claim in an event bundle, proving that neither favorable nor unfavorable formal contradictions were selectively suppressed.
status: Event matching can be wrong, and semantic contradiction requires judgment. The proof certifies inclusion and formal classification, never truth.
why: Inquiries that preserve uncertainty instead of manufacturing consensus.

title: Amendment Without Exposure — proposal
open: Before a cutoff, a witness may replace permitted fields; recipients see the authorized current version without learning who edited, when, or how often.
status: Shield already supports modification; the proposed addition is concealed revision linkage with auditable release semantics. Published copies remain.
why: Corrections that do not become new targeting signals.

title: Patient Cross-Examination Relay — proposal
open: Endpoints exchange fixed-rate padded traffic. Questioners receive answers—or an indication that none was ready—only at fixed epochs.
status: Cover hides transport activity, not answer semantics from the questioner. Delays, outages, and adaptive questioning need a composable leakage model.
why: Follow-up scrutiny without broadcasting a witness’s daily schedule.

title: Content-Blind Disruption Tribunal — proposal
open: Revoke a submission credential only for a proved protocol violation, such as malformed traffic or unauthorized duplicate writes.
status: Omission and network failure require explicit synchrony assumptions; silence alone cannot establish culpability.
why: Testimony infrastructure with disruption control but no discretionary content-censorship switch.

title: Cohort-Bound Release Mixnet — proposal
open: Release a statement only in a batch meeting its contributor-chosen count and credential-composition conditions; otherwise retain it sealed.
status: Cohort size is not an anonymity theorem. Adversarial contributors and recognizable content can collapse protection; failure behavior also leaks.
why: Small communities can refuse publication that would isolate a surviving witness.
key_works: Secure allegation escrows; accountable anonymous groups.

title: Source-Independent Testimony Lottery — proposal
open: Sample admitted accounts under a frozen distribution independent of source identity or content, except declared strata.
status: Admission can be biased and unfavorable draws aborted. Prohibit redraws; correct sampling is not necessarily unbiased conditional on completion.
why: An overwhelmed inquiry can distribute attention without allowing one institution to curate the record.

title: Unlinkable Omission Challenge — proposal
open: A depositor demonstrates that an acknowledged, eligible ciphertext was absent from the committed processing set.
status: Transferable receipts can become coercion evidence. Designated-verifier intake handling plus aggregate omission verdicts is one possible mitigation; collaborative proof generation alone is not nontransferability.
why: Witnesses can challenge quiet suppression of inconvenient evidence.

title: Treaty Circuit Court — proposal
open: Evaluate an agreed deterministic rule on authenticated committed inputs. Acknowledged dispute flags or missing attestations trigger a defined outside-scope result.
status: The circuit cannot discover unreported factual disputes, interpret unrestricted law, or compel physical enforcement.
why: Settlement of encoded deadlines, arithmetic obligations, and other agreed predicates without recognizing another institution’s court.

title: Ambiguity-Envelope Court — proposal
open: Commit a finite family of plausible rule interpretations; issue a disposition only when all produce the same authorized result.
status: The interpretation family must be fixed beforehand and cannot capture arbitrary meanings. Large families are expensive; ambiguity itself leaks information.
why: Automated common ground despite unresolved constitutional, historical, or theological differences.

title: Minimal-Counterexample Appeal — proposal
open: An appeal proves an admissible counterexample to one committed premise or computation step; release only the invalidated clause identifier.
status: Clause identity can expose a sensitive fact. Admissibility and credibility need agreed rules; “minimal” does not automatically mean private.
why: Narrow correction of demonstrable errors without transferring an opponent’s evidence.

title: Hidden-Remedy Pareto Court — proposal
open: Return a feasible remedy and prove that no permitted alternative weakly improves every submitted utility while strictly improving at least one.
status: Submitted preferences can be strategic. Pareto efficiency for those preferences establishes neither justice nor proportionality.
why: Restitution forms that public positional bargaining might never discover.

title: Venue-Before-Facts Router — proposal
open: Hidden jurisdictional attributes select one committed procedure or “no agreed venue”; rejected venues receive no case.
status: A unique destination can reveal facts, and routing rules can discriminate. Cryptography cannot create legitimate jurisdiction.
why: Redress without first disclosing a sensitive dispute to every rival authority.

title: Fact-Sensitivity Certificate — proposal
open: For committed admissible input ranges, certify outcome invariance or the existence of two admissible assignments producing different dispositions.
status: Universal checks may be intractable, and admissible ranges may encode bias. The sensitivity result itself leaks.
why: Formal arbitration that can identify when human fact-finding is necessary.
key_works: Publicly auditable MPC, composed with checked solver certificates.

title: Sealed-Precedent Consistency Gate — proposal
open: Equivalent cases under an agreed feature relation require consistent dispositions or an authorized, scoped exception.
status: The equivalence relation is normative. Missing or selectively committed precedents remain an input-governance problem.
why: Confidential settlements can support procedural consistency instead of secret double standards.

title: Appeal-Latched Escrow Judgment — proposal
open: Escrow releases only after a valid disposition and resolution of every acknowledged timely appeal.
status: Filing censorship needs its own challenge mechanism. Availability, escrow enforcement, and abort recovery are additional assumptions.
why: A party cannot use the system to execute an award while suppressing an acknowledged appeal.

title: Survivor Branch Certificate — proposal
open: A claimant proves an attested path to a qualifying historical-event credential under a published kinship policy.
status: Attestations establish recorded relationships, including recognized adoption—not historical truth or moral worth. Destroyed records and dishonest issuers remain.
why: Scholarships or memorial access without identifiable survivor-family registers.

title: Equal-Kin Edge — proposal
open: Certify the permitted kinship equivalence class without revealing whether adoption, guardianship, or biological descent supplied a qualifying edge.
status: Agreement about qualifying relations is governance. Unequal documentation can exclude applicants, and eligibility can still imply background information.
why: Benefits that respect recognized families without exposing adoption or guardianship.

title: Ash-Witness Enrollment — proposal
open: Require distinct authorized witnesses, with agreed institutional diversity, to attest the same hidden relationship claim.
status: Institutional diversity does not prove independent memory or truthfulness. Failure to reach a quorum must not become a negative historical finding.
why: Access for families whose documents disappeared through displacement or deliberate destruction.

title: Family Entitlement Algebra — proposal
open: Split a committed family benefit into hidden claimant-controlled shares whose total respects an authorized succession rule.
status: Conservation covers the enrolled roster, not unknown relatives. Contested enrollment and corrections require explicit rules for freezing or revising allocations.
why: Compensation inheritance across estranged and dispersed families.

title: Unlinkable Claim Constellation — proposal
open: Each program learns only whether its proposed payment fits the joint cap; the claimant alone receives the remaining balance.
status: Timing and unusual amounts can identify people. Enrollment, recovery, and atomic balance updates require explicit threat models.
why: Portable support across countries and institutions without routine cross-program tracking.

title: Lineage Repair Cascade — proposal
open: A signed correction invalidates stale downstream eligibility while permitting repaired or unaffected paths to refresh privately.
status: Efficient private refresh across enormous dependency graphs remains an integration target. Past disclosure cannot be undone, and clawbacks require policy.
why: Genealogical correction without turning an archival mistake into public stigma.

title: Veiled Eligibility Union — proposal
open: Accept multiple authorized routes—such as descent, recognized kinship, or sponsorship—while revealing only that some route qualifies.
status: Alternative routes must be real and receive equivalent treatment. Distinct timing, expiry, recovery, or outside knowledge can expose the route.
why: Assistance for survivor families without labeling all recipients as such.

title: Mutual Kinship Beacon — proposal
open: Reveal whether authenticated ancestor sets intersect within an agreed generation range; contact disclosure requires separate consent.
status: A match reveals a relationship. Repeated guesses require authorization limits, documentary errors remain, and abort must never force identity disclosure.
why: Reconnection without a public map of survivor lineages.

title: Jamarat Counterflow Covenant — proposal
open: Private group sizes, acceptable windows, and consented or independently justified separation constraints produce private crossing tickets and a public compliance proof.
status: Integer optimization must scale, and modelled safety depends on realistic crowd bounds and compliance. Offline signatures alone cannot prevent copied-ticket redemption.
why: Joint movement planning among rival pilgrimage institutions.

title: Arafat Sunset Release Envelope — proposal
open: Compute dispatch windows feasible for every arrival profile within committed uncertainty intervals; release only each operator’s instructions.
status: Private robust optimization must support safe rolling updates. An operator’s own instructions can imply another group’s delay; unmodeled behavior remains outside the guarantee.
why: Delay-tolerant departure planning without central possession of all schedules.

title: Mina Three-Way Exchange — proposal
open: Find a consented cycle of capacity or accommodation exchanges, privately proving acceptance and resource conservation.
status: Repeated hypothetical swaps reveal preferences. Atomicity concerns the reservation ledger; providers must honor it, and MPC cannot compel simultaneous physical execution.
why: Adjustments without broadcasting bargaining positions or requiring direct bilateral negotiation.

title: Muzdalifah Exception Cloak — proposal
open: Issue an alternative movement window after proving an accepted exception predicate, hiding diagnosis and the qualifying credential branch.
status: The assigned service can itself identify the exception. Credential policy and service design must address this; visible accommodations remain visible.
why: Private accommodation of health, disability, or other authorized needs.

title: Rite-Order Private Witness — proposal
open: A private itinerary satisfies one authorized rule system from an agreed family and all shared capacity constraints, while hiding the selected rule branch.
status: Communities must validate their rule encodings. Formal compatibility does not establish religious validity.
why: Coordination across accepted ritual interpretations without exposing personal adherence.

title: Crowd Slack Without Counts — proposal
open: Release a conservative additional-admission band, proving that it preserves committed capacity reserves.
status: Exact repeated slack answers can reconstruct demand. The leakage account must include denials, rounding, and physical observations.
why: Useful gate decisions with less centralized operational intelligence.

title: Limited-Disruption Rerouting — proposal
open: After an authenticated closure, issue revised private tickets and certify that at most a specified number changed while agreed protections remain.
status: A bounded repair may not exist. Failure needs an explicit result and a pre-agreed physical fallback.
why: Auditable rerouting without disclosure of complete itineraries.

title: Hajj Ticket Epoch Lock — proposal
open: Replacement schedules activate only after a guard interval covering clock skew and clearance of previously authorized movements.
status: Split views, delayed updates, and fallback activation must not create overlapping occupancy. Secret sharing supplies neither consensus nor a trustworthy physical clock.
why: Private allocation changes despite intermittent connectivity and hostile operators.

title: Equal-Precedence Rotation — proposal
open: Allocate passage windows subject to private cumulative-delay balances and a publicly chosen rotation rule.
status: Comparable burdens and authenticated delays require agreement and measurement. The rotation rule’s fairness is a premise, not a cryptographic conclusion.
why: Repeated arrangements that cannot silently turn temporary priority into permanent precedence.

title: Multi-Calendar Collision Oracle — proposal
open: Private event intervals generate only coarse periods requiring coordination, withholding participating institutions and routes.
status: A rare observance may be identifiable from a conflict flag. Repeated forecasts and uncertain dates require explicit leakage analysis.
why: Early coordination while institutions retain their own calendars and date-setting procedures.

title: Doorway Lease Without Title — proposal
open: A capability permits one specified action at an agreed doorway during one interval and proves the required custodial approvals.
status: The credential’s institutional meaning must remain narrow. Physical enforcement and key governance are external; the credential creates no legitimate title.
why: Small, reversible agreements despite unresolved larger claims.

title: Headway Under Secret Delays — proposal
open: Two groups learn whether their committed plans preserve agreed headway for every timing realization within accepted uncertainty sets.
status: Declared timing bounds must be credible. Repeated narrowing can reveal a schedule, and mathematical separation does not control actual movement.
why: Local crossing verification without surrendering routes or full timetables.

title: Acoustic Truce Budget — proposal
open: Under a jointly specified acoustic model, privately allocate acceptable sound intervals and levels; reveal each institution’s permissions.
status: Models, measurement locations, and acceptable burdens need agreement. Audible events remain observable regardless of transcript privacy.
why: Specific soundscape agreements without publishing future observance plans.

title: Affiliation-Blind Passage — proposal
open: Prove a valid reservation and eligibility under an authorized rule, hiding the issuer branch and destinations beyond the current checkpoint.
status: Clothing, companions, routes, and timing may expose affiliation. Small eligibility classes and issuer metadata must be addressed.
why: Shared access systems that need not build religious-affiliation registers.

title: Counterfactual Delay Appeal — proposal
open: Certify that some feasible alternative improves the appellant’s burden by an agreed threshold while preserving others’ protected conditions.
status: Repeated threshold appeals become a preference oracle. Large combinatorial instances need efficient proofs and a fixed appeal budget.
why: Scheduling appeals grounded in verifiable alternatives rather than compelled calendar disclosure.

title: Sanctuary Escape Reserve — proposal
open: Every confidential allocation must preserve an agreed escape reserve across a bounded family of emergency scenarios.
status: A conservative physical model needs validation. Arithmetic cannot certify unmodeled crowds, obstructed infrastructure, or compliance during an emergency.
why: Private everyday scheduling with an auditable emergency-access floor.

title: Reciprocal Gesture Seal — proposal
open: Precommitted messages become releasable only after all required matching authorizations exist.
status: A ledger alone is only an audit log. Fair release requires specified escrow, availability, timing, and corruption assumptions; earlier abort remains possible.
why: Reciprocal acknowledgments or invitations without unilateral prepublication exposure.

title: Graduated Reciprocity Ratchet — proposal
open: A committed state machine advances only when each side satisfies the current authenticated conditions, withholding unused future concessions.
status: Attestations do not prove physical performance. Abort can signal readiness, and rigid stages can conflict with changing consent.
why: Reconciliation that accumulates verifiable progress without demanding total initial disclosure.

title: Noncanceling Responsibility Ledger — proposal
open: Obligations carry private beneficiary scopes and remedy types; opposing obligations cannot cancel without the required beneficiaries’ explicit conversion authorization.
status: Types and releases need agreement. Cryptography cannot establish moral equivalence, factual performance, or control off-system settlements.
why: Mutual acknowledgment without automatic arithmetic equivalence between different harms.

title: Acknowledgment Without Endorsement — proposal
open: A receipt proves possession of an exact statement and completion of a named mechanical check; it conveys no agreement, understanding, or admission.
status: Digital checks cannot establish attention or comprehension and can be outsourced. Public actors may still misrepresent the receipt.
why: Evidence that grievances reached authorized channels without forcing endorsement.

title: Forgiveness Capability Firewall — proposal
open: A person’s token authorizes specified interactions and cannot satisfy software checks for unrelated settlement, testimony release, or waiver.
status: Type separation governs software, not legal interpretation or social pressure. Other people can still mischaracterize participation.
why: Participation in reconciliation without platform-level surrender of unrelated rights.
key_works: Designated-verifier proofs; Shield’s mutable consent-related records.

title: Safe-Continuation Discovery — proposal
open: For a bounded state machine, certify a contingent policy preserving private limits under declared disruptions and withdrawal options.
status: A winning policy may not exist. Environmental moves, withdrawal rights, state-space costs, and output-trace leakage require explicit treatment.
why: Initial cooperation with checkable protections against later procedural traps.
key_works: Publicly auditable MPC; zero-knowledge planning as an adjacent proof target.

title: Non-Accusatory Incident Fuse — proposal
open: Secret reports meeting a committed corroboration predicate produce a bounded pause or verification request; attribution requires a separate process.
status: Coordinated false reports may satisfy a weak predicate. Pauses can be weaponized; limits and a contest mechanism are necessary.
why: Fragile processes can respond to alarming information before accusations harden.
key_works: Secure allegation escrows; publicly auditable MPC.

title: Exit-Without-Betrayal Certificate — proposal
open: Certify which committed obligations are completed, consensually released, or pending, without exposing negotiations or asserting moral innocence.
status: Exit rules can become unjust as circumstances change. Contested physical obligations remain unresolved, and an adversary may block certification.
why: Institutions can leave without either side silently rewriting the process history.

title: Exculpation-Latched Disclosure — proposal
open: Accusatory release requires making all committed records matching the agreed exculpation predicate available to authorized defense recipients, with specified protections.
status: Guarantees cover committed records and encoded relevance only. Hidden evidence, witness danger, and guilt remain substantive questions.
why: The system cannot selectively disclose incriminating material while withholding formally linked rebuttals.

title: Cross-Bloc Corroboration Option — proposal
open: Reports satisfying an agreed diversity-of-attestation rule generate confidential follow-up eligibility; further disclosure requires fresh consent.
status: Credential diversity is not factual independence. False matching, strategic enrollment, and threshold-breaking withdrawals require careful treatment.
why: Witnesses can discover support across hostile institutions without creating a public accusation.

title: Adversarial Due-Process Aperture — proposal
open: Each authorized defense question receives a predetermined evidentiary view and a completeness proof relative to committed records.
status: Some accusations cannot be meaningfully challenged without identifying a source. The protocol must report incompatibility when protection and adequate scrutiny cannot coexist.
why: Protected testimony can be scrutinized through demonstrably consistent views.
key_works: Publicly auditable MPC; zero-knowledge selective disclosure.

title: Acquittal Repair Relay — proposal
open: An authenticated corrected disposition creates a linked notice in each authorized mailbox while hiding recipient lists and sealed evidence.
status: Availability is not human attention or belief. The system cannot erase copies or reach undisclosed onward recipients.
why: Verifiable correction propagation without publishing everyone connected to a case.

title: Appeal Reexecution Capsule — proposal
open: An authorized appeal applies a corrected rule to the original committed evidence plus explicitly admitted amendments.
status: Key custody, permissions, and assumptions must survive the appeal horizon. Correct execution cannot repair omitted evidence or legitimate a new rule.
why: Procedural correction across political transitions without exposing witnesses to successor governments.

title: Cumulative Disclosure Firewall — proposal
open: Within a finite declared adversary-knowledge model, authorize queries only if their possible outputs preserve specified uncertainty about protected attributes.
status: Unknown outside knowledge defeats universal claims. Adaptive refusals and exact inference can make analysis difficult or intractable.
why: Individually modest questions cannot silently reconstruct a dossier within the declared model.

title: Necessary-Disclosure Certificate — proposal
open: Among a finite menu of views, select one meeting a committed procedural sufficiency test at minimum declared disclosure cost.
status: Sufficiency and cost are negotiated judgments. Cross-field inference can invalidate additive privacy costs; richer optimization may be expensive.
why: An inquiry can explain formally why a date, location, or relationship had to be revealed.
key_works: Publicly auditable MPC; Otti’s optimization proofs.

title: Nontransferable Issuance Receipt — proposal
open: A designated recipient verifies issuance, but can simulate the proof transcript, so it does not publicly establish issuance or guilt.
status: Recipients can repeat the information, and coercers can control devices. Nontransferable evidence is narrower than secrecy or protection against defamation.
why: Private support or preliminary coordination without portable, authoritative-looking guilt tokens.

title: Blind Scarcity Settlement — proposal
open: Authenticated claims and a fixed budget produce private awards under an agreed allocation rule.
status: Fairness of the formula and authenticity of evidence remain human responsibilities. Tiny aggregates and payment rails can expose recipients; abort must not falsely finalize awards.
why: Auditable allocation without a central holder of sensitive claims.

title: Hidden Deed Collision — proposal
open: A claimant learns whether its enrolled claim overlaps another geometrically or genealogically, receiving an opaque dispute handle.
status: Historical boundaries need uncertainty semantics, and documents cannot decide legitimate title. Genuine-claim credentials must constrain parcel-probing attacks.
why: Early conflict handling without exposing families to targeted pressure.

title: Counterfactual Compensation Envelope — proposal
open: A fixed model family evaluates identical claims; recipients learn minimum and maximum awards and named components identical across all models.
status: Model families must be frozen before outputs. Repeated variants can reconstruct claims, and computational agreement establishes neither causal truth nor funding authority.
why: Payment of undisputed components while preserving disagreement about contested assumptions.

title: Nonwaiver Installment Receipt — proposal
open: A partial payment updates a hidden balance while preserving an explicit, policy-defined reservation of unresolved rights.
status: A receipt cannot make a clause legally effective. Interest, inheritance, disputed deductions, and interrupted payments require an agreed state machine.
why: Early reparations without platform-level conversion into undisclosed full settlement.

title: Reparation Reserve Curtain — proposal
open: At one accounting epoch, certify that committed, unencumbered reserves cover admitted hidden liabilities.
status: External encumbrances and complete liabilities require verification outside the circuit. Repeated solvency predicates reveal bounds; missing attestations must produce an uncertified epoch.
why: Credible funding promises without public claim registers.

title: Offset Without Association — proposal
open: Programs compute permitted monetary overlap for the same covered harm, withholding other claims and affiliations.
status: Harm equivalence is more than identity matching and needs appeals. Repeated adjustments can expose earlier awards; poor event identifiers reveal associations.
why: Coordination without a unified victim database.

title: Restitution Exchange Ring — proposal
open: Private acceptable alternatives produce disjoint, mutually acceptable exchange cycles.
status: Title, physical access, and fair completion require outside enforcement. Proposal outputs reveal preferences even when the search stays private.
why: Restitution packages without exposing bargaining positions or family histories.

title: Restitution Reversal Reserve — proposal
open: A provisional award contains a bounded hidden correction reserve; later authorized decisions may redirect only that portion.
status: Uncertainty and fraud need a real process. Clocks, decision credentials, and escrow enforcement remain assumptions; abort may delay release.
why: Earlier payments while limiting future hardship.

title: Century Baton — proposal
open: Transfer archive shares between changing generations without reconstruction or silent weakening of access rules.
status: Secure erasure, institutional diversity, migration, and recoverable handover must persist. Already compromised old ciphertexts cannot be rescued retrospectively.
why: Archives that outlive governments, religious administrations, and trustees.

title: Constitution-Locked Archive Migration — proposal
open: The replacement must refine the old disclosure behavior: protected inputs, recipients, query powers, repetition limits, and allowed failure or timing leakage.
status: Equal output ranges are insufficient, and unrestricted program equivalence is unavailable. Semantic exposure through permitted prose remains difficult.
why: Technological renewal that preserves contributors’ original boundaries.

title: Excerpt Passport — proposal
open: Publish an approved excerpt and proof that it is an allowed transformation of a committed archival record.
status: Exact wording can identify a speaker. Syntactic redaction does not establish semantic anonymity, and provenance is not truth.
why: Citation of protected evidence without unrestricted source inspection.

title: No Automatic Unsealing — proposal
open: Transition to a chosen successor policy only after authenticated succession conditions; the default transition preserves secrecy.
status: Death and succession are external facts. The system cannot infer new consent from the deceased; disputes and lost keys need previously agreed recovery procedures.
why: Posthumous research within contributor-chosen boundaries.

title: Hidden-Object Recovery Drill — proposal
open: Certify a defined retrievability assurance at fixed epochs and issue private repair tasks when redundancy becomes insufficient.
status: The extraction theorem must cover colluding stores, hidden challenges, and adaptive repair. Passing an audit guarantees neither future availability nor independent physical replicas.
why: Detection and repair of archival decay without opening sensitive collections.

title: Bounded Contradiction Map — proposal
open: Publish approved aggregate inconsistencies under machine-checkable predicates, such as mutually exclusive date intervals.
status: Contradiction is not proof of lying. Perspective, transcription, and uncertainty matter; omitted inputs must be represented as incomplete coverage.
why: Historians can prioritize disputed questions without publicizing vulnerable sources.

title: Nonresetting Historical Privacy Budget — proposal
open: Protected records retain a cumulative disclosure budget across replicas, researchers, policy versions, and generations.
status: The evolving neighboring-dataset relation must handle consent and linkage changes. Ordinary composition cannot repair a false identity-linkage model or erase prior outputs.
why: Historical research whose formal privacy promises survive administrative turnover.

title: Plural-Memory Invariant — proposal
open: For a predefined question, release unanimous support, absence of unanimity, or incomplete coverage across committed archival snapshots.
status: Agreement among selected records is not historical truth. Adaptive predicates can fingerprint dissenting archives; abstention must remain distinct from disagreement.
why: Shared statements alongside protected disagreement.

title: Treaty Readiness Barrier — proposal
open: Authenticated readiness conditions produce only authorization—or no authorization—for the next agreed civilian action.
status: Monitors must be accurate. A conjunction can reveal a holdout to colluders; missing inputs and abort do not prove anyone was unready.
why: Coordinated reconstruction commitments without exposing who was ready first.

title: Demobilization Count Without Roster — proposal
open: Release authorized aggregates of distinct, voluntarily enrolled people with current reintegration attestations; individuals privately prove their own eligibility.
status: Enrollment can be fabricated or misclassified. Endpoints and service cohorts need protection; aborted accounting must not automatically suspend essential assistance.
why: Funding reintegration without a broadly shared targeting register.

title: Destruction Token Cancellation — proposal
open: Count unique committed items carrying valid independently witnessed retirement certificates under the treaty’s accounting rule.
status: Inspectors must establish physical retirement. The proof covers declared items and cannot establish that undeclared inventory does not exist.
why: Bounded compliance evidence without transferring sensitive inventories.

title: Homecoming Capacity Match — proposal
open: Private preferences and authenticated housing or service capacities produce individually encrypted feasible offers.
status: Arithmetic feasibility is not physical safety. Preferences must remain revocable before acceptance; rare requirements may identify a family, and abort creates no relocation obligation.
why: Planning without public maps of intended return.

title: Reciprocal Return Option — proposal
open: Activate a reservation only with continuing household consent and independently attested local readiness; otherwise let it expire.
status: Readiness indicators cannot guarantee safety. Scarcity allocation and cancellation need agreed rules; observers may still detect activation.
why: Reversible planning instead of public promises people may fear to withdraw.
key_works: Anonymous credentials; MPC over private state.

title: Return-Neutral Aid Proof — proposal
open: For a committed policy and hidden circumstances, certify identical named benefits under “stay” and “return.”
status: Encoded equality cannot prevent intimidation, discretionary denial, or manipulated background attributes; it does not establish the policy’s overall fairness.
why: A checkable boundary against conditioning essential assistance on departure.

title: Civilian Peace Dividend — proposal
open: A committed pool pays agreed civilian beneficiaries when authenticated indicators meet predetermined thresholds, withholding individual monitor reports.
status: Metrics can distort behavior and monitors can be biased. Escrow must exist; essential aid must remain outside the conditional pool, including during abort.
why: Shared incentives without concentrating sensitive monitoring data.

title: Emergency-Power Expiry Seal — proposal
open: Exceptional access or inspection capabilities become invalid at a fixed deadline; renewal requires fresh authorization, while ordinary entitlements retain separate rules.
status: Verifiers and clocks must enforce expiry. Cryptography cannot compel relinquishment of physical power or prevent institutional bypass.
why: Temporary technical powers that cannot persist merely through procedural deadlock.

title: Blind Basin Compact — proposal
subfield: Common resources without a common trusted operator
open: Private forecasts, minimum-service commitments, and demand curves produce individual quotas with a public conservation proof.
status: Sensors and forecasts can fail; upstream actors can ignore quotas. The certificate establishes model execution, while credible measurement and physical enforcement remain external.
why: Water-sharing without a custodian trusted with every community’s vulnerabilities.

title: Grid Truce Dispatch — proposal
subfield: Common resources without a common trusted operator
open: Operators learn authorized boundary flows and local actions; a common proof establishes compliance with the committed electrical approximation and reserves.
status: A simplified model does not guarantee physical stability. Telemetry, model-error margins, and independent protection systems require engineering beyond cryptography.
why: Civilian electrical cooperation without exposing operational weaknesses.

title: Unadvertised Rescue Capacity — proposal
subfield: Common resources without a common trusted operator
open: Private capacity offers and minimal authorized clinical requirements produce patient-specific destinations, withholding regional inventories and unmatched requests.
status: Capacity changes rapidly, clinical suitability requires judgment, and inputs can be false. Receiving clinicians necessarily learn information needed for care.
why: Medical cooperation among communities afraid to reveal scarcity or surplus.

title: Reciprocal Public-Good Trigger — proposal
subfield: Common resources without a common trusted operator
open: Execute pledges when both an overall funding target and constituency floors hold, withholding donor identities and constituency totals.
status: Refundable escrow and payment finality need additional assumptions. Strategic withholding and artificial constituency splitting require incentive analysis.
why: Joint schools, sanitation, or restoration without a trusted fundraiser.

title: No-Pricelist Procurement — proposal
subfield: Common resources without a common trusted operator
open: Release the selected contract and each buyer’s own allocation and invoice, withholding losing bids and other demand curves.
status: Goods and delivery require outside verification. The chosen pricing rule may reveal a rival’s demand through a buyer’s own bill.
why: Collective purchasing without exposing institutional dependence.

title: Private Burden Ceiling — proposal
subfield: Common resources without a common trusted operator
open: Infrastructure cost shares must remain below privately evidenced affordability caps while satisfying an agreed funding rule.
status: Attestations may omit resources, and declared outside options can be strategic. Accounting predicates do not establish actual hardship.
why: Shared flood-control, sewage, or restoration projects despite financial distrust.

title: Compatibility Without Inventory — proposal
subfield: Common resources without a common trusted operator
open: Select a configuration satisfying all committed interoperability constraints, withholding rejected options and attributed incompatibilities.
status: Stale inventories and repeated queries can expose or fingerprint equipment. Formal compatibility still requires physical integration tests.
why: Shared warning, humanitarian communications, and utility interfaces across suspicious operators.

title: Silent Externality Settlement — proposal
subfield: Common resources without a common trusted operator
open: Authenticated bounded measurements produce private charges or credits, with public proof of the agreed formula and accounting balance.
status: Signed measurements can be false, strategically placed, or incomplete. Attribution and enforcement require agreement outside the circuit.
why: Environmental compacts without centralized industrial intelligence.

title: Coalition-Cut Compiler — proposal
open: Given possible coalitions, a network model, and outputs, derive conditions for confidentiality, correctness with abort, authorization, and achievable delivery.
status: Representing an access structure does not establish robust MPC. Cryptography cannot discover hidden common ownership or make a declared coalition model true.
why: Treaties that explicitly show which alliances could compromise them.

title: Refusal-Aware Privacy Ledger — proposal
open: Account for acceptance, refusal, timing classes, and released outputs across related protocols before permitting another query.
status: The target must compose selective abort and adaptive cross-protocol queries. It does not circumvent fairness impossibility.
why: Institutions cannot reset disclosure budgets by relabeling failed attempts.

title: Witness-Safe Fault Proof — proposal
open: Name a culpable institutional key and violated rule while hiding the record and session within a fixed batch.
status: Non-framing and selective-abort privacy need proof. A deliberately unique fault can identify its victim despite ZK; timeouts require network assumptions before implying blame.
why: Public fault accountability without automatic witness-location evidence.

title: Interpreter Pluralism Pact — proposal
open: Independent implementations must prove conformity to the same bounded treaty semantics and numeric conventions.
status: Functionally equivalent circuits do not necessarily interoperate. Translation validation, backend interoperability, and overflow behavior require verification; matching code hashes are insufficient.
why: Cooperation without a shared vendor or opaque reference executable.

title: Cross-Treaty Identity Firewall — proposal
open: Census, voting, lineage, and testimony entitlements remain unlinkable across purposes except for expressly authorized joins.
status: The proof must cover malicious issuers, chosen schemas, shared recovery, and lifetime composition. Physical observations remain outside cryptographic unlinkability.
why: Claiming restitution need not create a searchable political or testimonial profile.

title: Assumption-Diversity Covenant — proposal
open: Preserve advertised secrecy whenever at least two of three designated candidates remain secure for the required parties under the declared failure model.
status: An OT combiner does not protect the whole stack. Distinct assumptions need not fail independently, and unrestricted one-of-two black-box robustness cannot be presumed.
why: Long-lived agreements less dependent on one mathematical foundation.

title: Victim-Selectable Everlasting Exit — proposal
open: After required deletion certificates verify, continuing computation excludes the selected record; the post-exit view is simulatable from surviving inputs and permitted prior outputs.
status: Everlasting security transfer and deletion composition already exist. The proposed extension is efficient selective withdrawal with shared state and changing committees; deletion can be refused.
why: A route toward confidentiality after later institutional capture.

title: Treaty Continuation Without Replay — proposal
open: Restart from one committed history preserving accepted inputs, consumed permissions, and already released outputs; reject alternate histories.
status: Recovery must account for early outputs, stale shares, and unavailable parties. Preserving privacy does not guarantee progress.
why: Long proceedings that survive crashes and operator replacement without duplicated benefits or disclosures.
